input.question: How did the American Southern accent develop?
input.ground_truth: It's more the other way around, and relates to the question "When did American English break from British English?". At first American and British English were the same, but then British English developed into what it is today. American English has not changed as much, and is actually closer to British English of 200 years ago. American Southern has been even slower to change (because of the relative isolation of the speakers), and is even closer to British English of that time!

Okay! Imagine a long, long time ago, people from different places came to live in the southern part of America. Some came from England, some from Africa, and some from other parts of Europe.

As they all lived together, they started talking a little bit differently from people in the north. They mixed their old ways of speaking with new words they learned. Over many, many years, this made a special way of talking—called the Southern accent.

So, the Southern accent grew because lots of different people with different ways of talking lived together and shared their words and sounds for a very long time. That’s how it developed!
